messages.subject: Question Using Config File
parts:
Hello, 

I just have a quick question when running the config file on a new set of gt3x files. If using a sleep diary, do I need to specify the filepath in my code? Do I need to update file paths in the config file as well? 

Thank you!

#Example code

GGIR(
            datadir = " filepath",
            outputdir = " filepath",
            congfigfile = " filepath"
# Do I need this too? loglocation = " filepath" )

messages.author: e0169f921473cc94
messages.subject: Re: Question Using Config File
parts:
Yes, if you want to use a sleep diary, you must pass a file to GGIR using the loglocation argument. 

I think if you're using the configfile argument then you would want to ensure your config.csv contains a filepath entry for the loglocation.

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Question Using Config File
parts:
Dear Reagan,

I just noticed I did not reply to your message from August. You have two options:
  1. Specify all your non-default parameters via the GGIR function call in your R script, including parameter loglocation, but do not fiddle with config.csv because config.csv is just a log of how GGIR combines your function arguments, its internal defaults and the information in the previous GGIR function run. Any parameter specified in your R script will overrule whatever is specified in the config.csv and after the analysis the value will be overwritten in the config.csv file.
  2. Only use the config.csv file, for example if you want to replicate a previous analysis.  Here, you will have to specify file paths such as datadir and outputdir via the GGIR function call but all other parameters no longer need to be specified.

For details see: https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/chapter2_Pipeline.html#configuration-file-

Thanks,

Vincent
